item.title: #3584347: Deprecate and replace system_admin_compact_mode()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +259/−101 · php +155/−70 · js +78 · yml +12/−6 · css +8 · twig +6/−25
  • Diff: 3e3315d
  • Discussion: #3584347 · 11 contributors · 72 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Admin pages such as the permissions page offer a "compact mode" that hides field descriptions to reduce clutter. This used to be implemented server-side: clicking the toggle loaded the /admin/compact/{mode} route, which set a Drupal_visitor_admin_compact_mode cookie (with a system.site:admin_compact_mode config fallback), and every request re-rendered the page accordingly. That mechanism has been deprecated and replaced with a purely client-side implementation: toggling compact mode now happens instantly via JavaScript and localStorage, with no page reload and no cookie or config lookup on the server.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Config change: system.site:admin_compact_mode config key is deprecated in 11.5.0, removed from 12.0.0, and cleared by the new system_post_update_clear_admin_compact_mode_config() update function.
  • Theme change: Admin block templates (system-admin-block-content.html.twig and the claro/gin equivalents) no longer receive a compact boolean variable; description elements are now always rendered and marked with a data-admin-compact-collapsible attribute that CSS hides based on a data-admin-compact-mode attribute on <html>.
  • API change: system_admin_compact_mode() and SystemController::compactPage() (route system.admin_compact_page) are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in Drupal 12.0.0, with no server-side replacement.
  • Deprecation: Admin compact mode moved entirely to the client: the system.site:admin_compact_mode config key and the cookie/config based toggle are deprecated in favor of a localStorage flag set purely in JavaScript.

Technical details

The old flow relied on system_admin_compact_mode() reading a cookie (falling back to system.site:admin_compact_mode config) and controllers/preprocess functions like SystemAdminThemePreprocess::preprocessAdminBlockContent() and UserPermissionsForm::buildForm() conditionally omitting description markup server-side. Both system_admin_compact_mode() and SystemController::compactPage() now call @trigger_error() and are marked @deprecated in 11.5.0 for removal in 12.0.0, with no replacement (see the linked change record 3588109). The admin_compact_mode key is stripped from system.site.yml defaults and cleared from existing sites via system_post_update_clear_admin_compact_mode_config().

The replacement lives entirely in a new system/drupal.system.admin_compact library (system.admin_compact.js + .css). It sets a data-admin-compact-mode attribute on the document root from a Drupal.admin.compact_mode localStorage value before behaviors attach (to avoid flicker), and toggles it on click of any [data-admin-compact-toggle] element. Description elements that used to be conditionally rendered are now always rendered but wrapped with data-admin-compact-collapsible, hidden purely via the CSS rule :root[data-admin-compact-mode] [data-admin-compact-collapsible] { display: none; }. Drupal\Core\Render\Element\SystemCompactLink::preRenderCompactLink() no longer builds a URL to the toggle route; it renders a static # link carrying data-admin-compact-toggle that the new behavior intercepts. An accessibility follow-up to turn this link into a proper switch/button is tracked in #3593539.

Upgrade

If a theme overrides system-admin-block-content.html.twig (or the claro/gin versions) and checks the old compact variable, remove that check. Descriptions are now always passed through; mark the collapsible element instead, matching core:

<dd class="list-group__description" data-admin-compact-collapsible>{{ item.description }}</dd>

Replace any calls to system_admin_compact_mode() or links to /admin/compact/{mode}: there is no server-side replacement. Compact mode is now a purely client-side localStorage flag (Drupal.admin.compact_mode), toggled by attaching data-admin-compact-toggle to a clickable element and depending on the system/drupal.system.admin_compact library.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 12, 2026
  • First commit: August 12, 2026 (4 months later)
  • Last commit: August 30, 2026 (17 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • znerol
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • andypost (Skilld)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • godotislate
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • kentr
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • longwave-bot

Collaboration

The design shifted during review. znerol originally proposed moving compact mode entirely into localStorage, but andypost cautioned that server-side controllers still rely on knowing the compact state, questioning whether a client-only replacement was feasible. nicxvan then built an MR implementing the localStorage approach anyway, noting "all of the core interactions with this do it server side", and mstrelan separately suggested making it a per-user account preference instead (similar to Gin theme's appearance setting). nicxvan reported discussing the tradeoffs in Slack with catch and andypost before settling on the final approach, crediting them and Godotislate for help working out the details.

item.title: #3580733: Views status field triggers a PHP 8.5 deprecation on /admin/people
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +447/−8 · php +438 · twig +9/−8
  • Diff: 51ff2c2
  • Discussion: #3580733 · 15 contributors · 61 comments
  • Followers: 22
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 15 contributors

Summary

On sites using core's experimental default_admin theme, visiting admin pages built from Views status fields (such as /admin/people) triggered a PHP 8.5 deprecation warning, "Using null as an array offset is deprecated", because the "Published"/"Unpublished" badge template tried to look up a translation using a language code that could be null. The same faulty logic also meant the published/unpublished badge could show the wrong color on views not based on nodes (for example taxonomy term listings), since it relied on a variable that only exists for node-based views. Both problems are fixed: the warning no longer appears, and the badge now reflects the correct publication state for any publishable entity type shown in a status field.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The default_admin theme's views-view-field--status.html.twig template no longer resolves the row's translated entity itself; it now receives a computed is_published boolean/null variable from a new preprocess hook, and no longer receives an entity variable.

Technical details

The old views-view-field--status.html.twig template inlined Twig logic to fetch the row's entity translation via row._entity.getTranslation(row.node_field_data_langcode) before checking isPublished(). node_field_data_langcode is a row property that only exists for node-based views, so on other views (or monolingual sites) it evaluated to NULL, which is what triggered the deprecation inside ContentEntityBase::hasTranslation(), and also silently produced the wrong publication state for non-node entities like taxonomy terms.

The fix moves this logic out of the template entirely. A new hook_preprocess_HOOK() implementation, PreprocessHooks::preprocessViewsViewFieldStatus() (theme suggestion views_view_field__status, which fires for any views field with the machine ID status on any entity type), resolves the row's entity through the field handler's own EntityField::getEntity() (respecting configured relationships via row._relationship_entities), and only sets a boolean is_published variable when the field's underlying entity field type is boolean. Otherwise is_published is NULL. The template was simplified to branch purely on is_published: TRUE renders the marker--published span, FALSE renders the plain marker span, and NULL renders the raw output with no marker at all, so fields that aren't a real published flag (e.g. views_test_data.status handled by the boolean plugin) pass through unaffected.

Because the entity is now resolved through the field handler, translation handling follows the view's configured rendering language instead of a hardcoded node-specific row property, fixing the mismatch for non-node views. Follow-up issues #3608223 and #3619121 were opened to move this kind of status-badge formatting into a proper Views field formatter rather than being hardcoded in the theme layer.

Upgrade

Themes that override core/themes/default_admin/templates/views/views-view-field--status.html.twig need to update their copy: the template no longer receives an entity variable and instead receives is_published (TRUE, FALSE, or NULL):

{% if is_published is null %}
  {{ output -}}
{% elseif is_published %}
  <span class="marker marker--published">{{ output -}}</span>
{% else %}
  <span class="marker">{{ output -}}</span>
{% endif %}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 22, 2026
  • Committed: August 29, 2026 (5 months and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • penyaskito (Acquia)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • idebr (iO)
  • jurgenhaas (LakeDrops)
  • boromino (LakeDrops)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

The fix went through several rounds of design disagreement before landing. penyaskito's initial proposal was to simply delete the translation lookup from the template, but berdir and alexpott argued the theme layer should not be resolving entity translations at all, and considered removing the status badge feature from default_admin entirely (with alexpott noting it should be reintroduced later with the multilingual issue fixed properly). jurgenhaas then produced MR!16557, moving the logic into a preprocess hook that computes a boolean published state; boromino reviewed it and suggested extracting named helper methods (getResultRowEntity(), isPublishedStatusField()) for clarity, which jurgenhaas applied. godotislate then explored two further alternatives, MR!16768 (preprocess using the field handler's entity resolution) and MR!16769 (template-only), after finding the original approach didn't handle entities like user that lack a published key or EntityPublishedInterface. berdir pushed back against using getFieldMap() in MR!16768 due to performance concerns raised in #3565128, so godotislate removed it in favor of calling EntityField::getEntity() directly. The group ultimately converged on MR!16768 as the pragmatic minimal fix, with berdir and jurgenhaas agreeing to defer the "proper" solution (a configurable Views boolean formatter) to follow-up issues #3608223 and #3619121.

item.title: #2012976: Deprecate user_logout() and user_login_finalize() and replace with a service
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +430/−71 · php +427/−71 · yml +2 · txt +1
  • Diff: accb9ca
  • Discussion: #2012976 · 28 contributors · 133 comments
  • Followers: 44
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 28 contributors

Summary

Drupal has deprecated the long-standing procedural functions user_login_finalize() and user_logout() in favour of two new services. Logging a user in or out still works exactly the same way for site visitors; this change is about how module code performs those actions. Any custom or contributor code that calls these functions directly will keep working but will trigger a deprecation notice, and should switch to the new services before Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: user_login_finalize() and user_logout() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and will be removed in drupal:13.0.0; use the new LoginFinalizer/LogoutFinalizer services instead.
  • New API: New final services Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer (finalizeLogin()) and Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer (finalizeLogout()) registered in user.services.yml.

Technical details

The procedural logic previously living in user_login_finalize() and user_logout() (session regeneration, updating the last-login timestamp, invoking hook_user_login()/hook_user_logout(), destroying the session, and logging) has been moved verbatim into two new final readonly classes, Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer::finalizeLogin() and Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer::finalizeLogout(). Both are plain services (no interfaces: an interface was originally proposed but dropped after berdir questioned the need for a swappable API with no known use case) declared in user.services.yml. The old functions now just emit an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and delegate to the new services.

All core call sites were switched to constructor-injected dependencies instead of calling the global functions: UserAuthenticationController, UserController, UserLoginForm, UserLogoutConfirm, RegisterForm, and install.core.inc. Each affected constructor gained new optional LoginFinalizer/LogoutFinalizer parameters defaulting to NULL, with a deprecation notice thrown when omitted so that existing subclasses keep working until the parameter becomes required. MaintenanceModeSubscriber, which runs on every request, injects the logout service lazily via #[AutowireServiceClosure(LogoutFinalizer::class)] rather than eagerly resolving it in the constructor.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions:

// Before
user_login_finalize($account);
user_logout();

// After
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer::class)->finalizeLogin($account);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer::class)->finalizeLogout();

Prefer constructor injection of Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer and/or Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer where possible.

If you subclass UserAuthenticationController, UserController, UserLoginForm, UserLogoutConfirm, or RegisterForm and call their constructors directly, pass the new $loginFinalizer/$logoutFinalizer arguments to avoid deprecation notices; they will become required in a future release.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 5, 2013
  • First commit: August 27, 2026 (13 years later)
  • Last commit: August 28, 2026 (1 day and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • ParisLiakos
  • dawehner
  • andypost (Skilld)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • lauriii (Acquia)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • znerol
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • kristiaanvandeneynde (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

This task sat open for over a decade before landing. Late in its life, catch and longwave pushed back on the design, questioning whether bundling login/logout into one service with seven dependencies made sense, and whether an event-based approach would be more flexible than a final service. berdir explained the real motivation (moving one of the last .module-level procedural calls out of controllers so .module files only need loading when a hook actually fires) and argued against duplicating the existing login/logout hooks with events. znerol sketched out a longer-term vision for a unified login/logout API with pluggable authentication mechanisms, but the group (heddn, kim.pepper) agreed to keep this issue narrowly scoped and defer that redesign. Based on the feedback, kim.pepper split the single service into separate LoginFinalizer and LogoutFinalizer classes and removed the interfaces after berdir pointed out core has moved away from adding interfaces without a concrete use case. TFA maintainer cmlara flagged that contrib modules call user_login_finalize() directly for non-form logins, which shaped the decision to keep the deprecated procedural wrappers rather than removing them outright.</collaboration> <parameter name="ai_disclosures">[]

item.title: #3610503: Optimize StorageCopyTrait::replaceStorageContents()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +27/−14 · php +27/−14
  • Diff: 7230379
  • Discussion: #3610503 · 3 contributors · 19 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Importing configuration (for example via drush config:import) used to read each changed config object from the database one at a time, which could mean hundreds or thousands of individual queries on a site with a large config set. This change batches those reads into chunks of 500, cutting the number of queries down to a handful. The issue author measured a couple hundred milliseconds saved on a Umami config import, with larger savings expected on sites with more configuration. Combined with the related config file parsing cache improvements in #3591680, this is expected to cut more than half the time off a typical drush config import.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in StorageCopyTrait::replaceStorageContents(), which is used whenever one config storage is synced into another (config import, config staging, etc.). Previously it looped over every config name and called $source_collection->read($name) and $target_collection->read($name) individually. Now it splits the list of names into array_chunk($names, 500) batches and calls readMultiple() once per chunk on both the source and target storage, then compares the in-memory arrays to decide whether to write or delete each item. For storage backends like DatabaseStorage, readMultiple() already issued a single SELECT ... WHERE name IN (...) query, so batching through it turns what could be thousands of round trips into a handful.

Making MemoryStorage::readMultiple() actually get exercised (it previously wasn't reachable from this code path) exposed a latent bug: it used array_intersect_key($this->config[$this->collection], array_flip($names)), which errors when the collection is empty or missing. It now delegates to read() per name, consistent with the class's other methods, which are only used in tests.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 12, 2026
  • Committed: August 28, 2026 (1 month and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

During review, godotislate found that the MemoryStorage change broke a test because that storage's readMultiple() was never previously invoked by this trait. catch pushed a revert plus a targeted fix, explaining the tradeoff between a straightforward foreach and more compact array handling. godotislate then suggested simplifying the foreach further via an MR suggestion, which catch applied.

item.title: #3380334: user_update_10000 fails on role with no data
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +33/−0 · php +33
  • Diff: 4fc1679
  • Discussion: #3380334 · 8 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 8 contributors

Summary

The user_update_10000 update hook (which removes non-existent permissions from roles during the Drupal 9 to 10 upgrade) could fatally error and halt the whole update batch if a site had a broken user.role.* configuration entry missing its permissions key entirely, for example due to an incomplete or corrupted config import in a site's history. Instead of crashing, the update hook now detects this case, logs a notice identifying the broken role, and skips it, letting the rest of the update process complete. The broken role's config is left in place (not deleted); administrators are pointed to the logs to investigate and clean it up manually.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In user_update_10000(), before calling array_diff($role_config->get('permissions'), $existing_permissions), the code now checks whether $role_config->get('permissions') returns NULL. If so, it logs a notice via \Drupal::logger('update') naming the role ($role_config->getName()) and reporting that it "has no permissions and should be removed", then continues to the next role instead of calling array_diff() with a null argument (which previously threw a TypeError under PHP 8's strict typing and aborted the update run).

The fix intentionally does not delete or repair the broken config, since removing configuration during an update hook was considered too risky without certainty about side effects; it only prevents the fatal error and surfaces the problem in the logs (admin/reports/dblog) for the site administrator to address separately.

Test coverage was added in UserUpdatePathTest, inserting a user.role.broken_role config row with empty serialized data (a:0:{}) directly into the config table, then asserting the update completes, the dblog notice appears, and the broken role's config row is left untouched in the database.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.title: #3587797: Move views data cache to cache_discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +8/−19 · php +8/−19
  • Diff: 7d8143e
  • Discussion: #3587797 · 7 contributors · 40 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Views builds a large in-memory data structure describing every database table exposed to Views (via hook_views_data()), and caches it both as one big entry and as many smaller per-table entries. Per-table entries were previously stored in the regular persistent cache (cache.default); they are now stored in the cache.discovery bin, which is chained with a fast, per-process backend like APCu when available. Since the set of tables is finite and rebuilt rarely, this lets repeat lookups for the same table on a page be served from local memory instead of the primary cache backend (Redis, database, etc.), reducing cache reads on pages that use Views. The single "all views data" entry stays in cache.default because it can be very large and the maintainers were concerned that pushing it into a fast in-memory bin could evict other cached data on large, multilingual sites.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() and cacheSet() are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in 12.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The initial commit simply swapped the constructor's #[Autowire] target for ViewsData::$cacheBackend from cache.default to cache.discovery, but this was reverted after berdir pointed out that the combined "all tables" entry can be tens of megabytes on sites with many languages or entity bundles, and forcing all of that into the chained-fast (APCu-backed) bin risked frequent APCu expunges and a performance regression rather than an improvement.

The follow-up perf commit instead adds a second injected backend, $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery), used only for the per-table cache entries in ViewsData::get(), while getData() keeps using $cacheBackend (cache.default) for the full "all tables" entry. A new ViewsData::CACHE_TAGS constant centralizes the views_data and config:core.extension cache tags used when setting either bin. The old protected cacheGet()/cacheSet() helpers, which always prefixed the langcode and used $cacheBackend, are no longer used internally and are deprecated with @trigger_error; callers should use the injected cache backends directly, following how the rest of the class now works.

Performance test fixtures (FrontPageTest, StandardPerformanceTestTrait, Umami/Standard profile test YAMLs) were updated to reflect the shift: discovery cache-get counts go up and default cache-get counts go down by the same amount, confirming per-table lookups now hit cache.discovery.

Upgrade

Subclasses or code relying on \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() or cacheSet() will get a deprecation notice starting in Drupal 11.5.0 and must stop using them before 12.0.0, since there is no direct replacement method. Interact with the injected $cacheBackend (cache.default, for the "all data" entry) or the new $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery, for per-table entries) directly instead:

// Before (deprecated):
$data = $this->cacheGet($cid);
$this->cacheSet($cid, $data);

// After, for per-table entries:
$data = $this->chainedFastBackend->get($this->prepareCid($cid));
$this->chainedFastBackend->set($this->prepareCid($cid), $data, Cache::PERMANENT, static::CACHE_TAGS);

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 30, 2026
  • First commit: April 30, 2026
  • Last commit: August 27, 2026 (3 months and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)

Collaboration

catch proposed moving the whole ViewsData cache to cache_discovery and alexpott committed it, but berdir flagged a regression risk: on large or heavily multilingual sites the combined "all tables" cache entry can be megabytes in size, and pushing that into APCu-backed chained-fast storage risks frequent expunges that hurt performance more broadly (citing real-world monitoring data from sites using an APCu-expunge sensor). alexpott reverted the commit the same day. berdir then measured actual cache entry sizes with a script run against a production-like Redis dataset, showing the "all tables" entries were an order of magnitude larger than the sum of per-table entries, and suggested moving only the per-table entries into the fast bin. catch implemented that split (two injected cache backends), and the two also floated further ideas (a hook_views_data_table()-style API, and not caching views data per-language) that were not pursued in this issue. berdir later reviewed again and preferred catch's simplified follow-up that dropped the old cacheGet/cacheSet helpers entirely in favor of calling the backends directly, calling it "much nicer."

item.title: #3472624: Ensure the UI dialog instance is valid in Drupal.dialog.resetSize
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +66/−3 · php +35 · js +31/−3
  • Diff: d0904d4
  • Discussion: #3472624 · 15 contributors · 36 comments
  • Followers: 21
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 15 contributors

Summary

Opening a modal dialog and closing it again very quickly (within about 20 milliseconds) could throw an uncaught JavaScript error, "cannot call methods on dialog prior to initialization; attempted to call method 'option'", because a scheduled dialog resize callback ran after the dialog had already been destroyed. This could interrupt other JavaScript on the page and was also causing intermittent failures in Drupal core's own JavaScript test suite. The fix ensures a resize that is still pending when a dialog closes is cancelled instead of running against a dialog that no longer exists.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Drupal.debounce() now returns a function that has a cancel() method, letting callers abort a scheduled invocation that has not run yet.

Technical details

The root cause was in misc/dialog/dialog.ajax.js: Drupal.dialog.resetSize is invoked via Drupal.debounce on window resize/scroll events, but the dialog:beforeclose handler only unbound those event listeners; it could not stop a resize call that had already been scheduled by debounce's internal setTimeout. By the time that timeout fired, the dialog's DOM element (and its jQuery UI instance) had already been removed, so calling .dialog('option', ...) on it threw.

The fix has two parts. misc/debounce.js's Drupal.debounce now returns a function that also carries a cancel() method, which clears the pending timeout so a scheduled call never runs. dialog.ajax.js stores the autoResize debounced function on the dialog element via $element.data('drupalAutoResize', autoResize) when the dialog opens, and its dialog:beforeclose handler now calls $(e.target).data('drupalAutoResize')?.cancel() before unbinding the resize/scroll handlers. As a defensive second layer, resetSize() also now bails out early if event.data?.$element?.data('ui-dialog') is falsy, i.e. the jQuery UI dialog instance is no longer present. Test coverage was added in DialogTest that opens a modal, triggers a resize, immediately closes the dialog, and asserts no JS errors are logged.

A change record (#3619513, referenced in comments) documents the new debounce().cancel() API for other core and contrib code that debounces callbacks tied to DOM elements that may be removed.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">The bug lingered for a long time with several reporters (grimreaper, goz, joseph.olstad, albeorte) confirming related but not-quite-matching symptoms with CKEditor and other dialog-triggering modules, and earlier MR attempts did not fully resolve it for them. The issue was escalated to Critical by longwave after noting in #16720832 that the flakiness had "got much worse" following #3515403 (the Selenium/Chrome upgrade), since it was now causing multiple JS test failures in core. Longwave then diagnosed the actual mechanism, that dialog:beforeclose unbinds handlers but cannot stop an already-scheduled debounced call, and implemented the debounce.cancel() fix with new test coverage, noting the diagnosis and fix were assisted by Claude Code. godotislate stress-tested the fix by repeating a previously flaky test 500 times without failure to confirm the intermittent failures were resolved before it was marked RTBC again.</collaboration> <parameter name="upgrade">

Fields displayed with the "Summary or trimmed" formatter could be cut off in the wrong place. If the underlying HTML used a non-breaking space ( ) instead of a plain space after a sentence's period, which CKEditor commonly does, the trimming logic did not recognize that period as a valid sentence break. item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +233/−40 · php +223/−40 · yml +10

Summary

Drupal has had two ways to run long tasks: the Queue API (normally only drained by cron) and the blocking Batch API. This issue adds a middle ground: an "instant queue runner" service that modules can hand a queue name to during a request, and a handful of items (5 by default) from that queue get processed right after the response has been sent to the browser, without blocking the user. This is opt-in per queue, not automatic for all queues, so existing sites see no behavior change until a module or contrib project starts using it. The maintainers point to use cases like closing a timing-attack window on the password reset form (#3316209), instant search indexing, and image style pre-warming as the reasons this landed now.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New instant_queue.config container parameter with a maximumItems key (default 5) caps how many items per queue the instant runner processes per request.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunnerInterface service lets modules register a queue name so a few of its items get processed right after the response is sent, instead of waiting for cron.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunner service implements InstantQueueRunnerInterface (a single registerQueue(string $queue_name): void method) and DestructableInterface, and is tagged needs_destruction so its destruct() runs during kernel.terminate. During a request, code that adds an item to a queue also calls registerQueue(); the runner just counts how many times each queue name was registered. In destruct(), for each registered queue it claims and processes up to min(maximumItems, $count) items (default maximumItems is 5, configurable via the instant_queue.config container parameter), stopping early if a worker throws SuspendQueueException.

To avoid duplicating the claim/process/exception-handling logic, the per-item processing loop previously inlined in Cron::processQueue() was extracted into a new Drupal\Core\Queue\QueueProcessTrait::processItem(), which handles DelayedRequeueException, RequeueException, SuspendQueueException, and generic \Throwable logging via Error::logException(). Both Cron and InstantQueueRunner now use this trait, so the exception semantics for queue workers are identical whether items run via cron or via the instant runner.

Nothing in core actually calls registerQueue() yet: no core queue was converted as part of this change, and integration with automated_cron was deliberately dropped from scope (comment #16451928) in favor of a simpler, opt-in-per-caller design without added concurrency protection. A follow-up (#3617085) proposes using it for field purging.

Upgrade

Modules that want a queue item processed shortly after the request that created it, instead of waiting for cron, can inject the new interface and register the queue name after adding the item:

public function __construct(
  protected QueueFactory $queueFactory,
  protected \Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunnerInterface $instantQueueRunner,
) {}

public function someMethod() {
  $this->queueFactory->get('my_queue')->createItem($data);
  $this->instantQueueRunner->registerQueue('my_queue');
}

Sites can change how many items get processed per queue per request by overriding the instant_queue.config container parameter (default maximumItems: 5) in a services.yml.

    // Moved logic from theme-settings.php here.

Summary

Drupal's user module used to send all of its notification emails (registration, password reset, account activated/blocked/canceled, cancellation confirmation) through a single internal function, _user_mail_notify(). Despite its underscore prefix marking it as internal, this function turned out to be called directly by dozens of contributed modules. Its logic has now been extracted into a new NotificationHandler service, one method per notification type (sendPasswordReset(), sendStatusActivated(), sendRegisterAdminCreated(), etc.). _user_mail_notify() itself still works exactly as before but is now formally deprecated, with a longer-than-usual grace period: it will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0 rather than sooner, specifically to give contrib maintainers time to update. Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: _user_mail_notify() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 for removal in drupal:13.0.0; its logic moved into the new (currently @internal) Drupal\user\NotificationHandler service.

Technical details

The new Drupal\user\NotificationHandler class lives in core/modules/user/src/NotificationHandler.php, is registered as an unaliased, autowired service (Drupal\user\NotificationHandler: ~), and is marked @internal with no interface: the maintainers deliberately did not want to commit to a public contract yet (see the long back-and-forth over whether to make it public, settled by an @internal-for-now compromise). It injects logger.channel.user and plugin.manager.mail as lazy \Closure values via #[AutowireServiceClosure] rather than eager services. All the old $op-dispatch logic from _user_mail_notify() is preserved in a protected sendToUser(string $op, UserInterface $account): ?bool method; the public methods (sendCancelConfirm(), sendPasswordReset(), sendStatusActivated(), sendStatusBlocked(), sendStatusCanceled(), sendRegisterAdminCreated(), sendRegisterNoApprovalRequired(), sendRegisterPendingApproval()) each wrap it and cast the result to bool, discarding the old NULL vs FALSE distinction that _user_mail_notify() still exposes for BC.

Calling this method currently throws Error: Call to undefined method Drupal\user\NotificationHandler::sendStatusCancelled(), which means deleting a user account with the "notify user by email" option checked will fatal rather than send the cancellation email.

item.description:

Summary

Drupal core's entity reference field API now uses PHP 8.4 property hooks to expose the entity and target_id properties on entity reference field items and item lists, instead of relying on PHP's __get()/__set() magic methods. This removes a fragile workaround that was needed to avoid a PHP bug where suspending a Fiber inside __get() could incorrectly trigger PHP's recursion guard, and it also fixes isset() checks on these properties inside a running Fiber, since PHP routes isset() through a property hook's get accessor but not through __isset().

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: entity and target_id on EntityReferenceItem and EntityReferenceFieldItemList are now declared as typed properties with PHP 8.4 property hooks instead of being handled by __get()/__set() magic methods; unset() on either property now throws Error: Cannot unset hooked property instead of silently clearing the value.

Technical details

Previously, EntityReferenceItemBase::__get() special-cased the entity property: when called while a Fiber was already running, it wrapped the call to parent::__get() in a new Fiber and manually pumped resume()/usleep() until it terminated, to dodge a PHP fiber/recursion-guard bug (php/php-src#14983). That override is now removed entirely; EntityReferenceItemBase is back to an empty class body.

Instead, EntityReferenceItem declares entity and target_id as typed properties (?EntityInterface $entity and string|int|null $target_id) using property hooks: the get hook delegates to the existing __get() logic and the set hook calls $this->set(). item.title: #3534109: Permanently maintain a sandbox directory in package_manager
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +629/−69 · php +623/−69 · yml +6
  • Diff: f31a5d8
  • Discussion: #3534109 · 6 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Package Manager (used by Automatic Updates, Project Browser, and other update tooling) used to copy the entire codebase into a fresh, randomly-named sandbox directory for every composer operation, then delete it afterwards. On hosts with limits on file operations (some shared/managed hosting providers), this churn of tens of thousands of file creates and deletes per operation could trip usage caps and lock accounts. Now Package Manager keeps a single sandbox directory around permanently and reuses it for every operation, so rsync only needs to copy files that actually changed instead of recreating the whole codebase each time. Stale sandboxes are cleaned up automatically during cron after a configurable number of days (14 by default), and the directory is still deleted immediately if a site turns off include_unknown_files_in_project_root, since leftover excluded files would otherwise never get removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New optional $settings['package_manager_max_sandbox_age'] (default 14 days) controls how long the now-persistent Package Manager sandbox directory is kept before cron deletes it.
  • API change: SandboxManagerBase::destroy() no longer deletes the sandbox directory (it stays on disk for reuse) and no longer queues cleanup via the package_manager_cleanup queue; getSandboxDirectory() now returns a fixed path (sandbox_directory, not a random per-stage name) and no longer throws \LogicException when called before the stage is created or claimed.

Technical details

The sandbox directory's name changed from a per-stage random token to a fixed sandbox_directory constant (SandboxManagerBase::COMPOSER_SANDBOX_DIRECTORY) under the site's staging root, so the same physical directory is reused across create/destroy cycles. SandboxManagerBase::destroy() was simplified to just release the lock and mark the stage available; it no longer deletes the directory or enqueues it to the package_manager_cleanup queue (the Cleaner queue worker itself is untouched, pending a possible follow-up to remove it). sandboxDirectoryExists() now means "the stage is actively claimed and its directory exists on disk," which is a different question from "does the directory physically exist," since a long-lived sandbox persists after destroy().

Because Composer Stager's stock StagingDirDoesNotExistInterface precondition expects an empty target, a new Drupal\package_manager\StagingDirDoesNotExist decorator was added that always reports the precondition as fulfilled, letting the sandbox be reused even though it already exists. Two new pieces of infrastructure manage the directory's lifecycle: EventSubscriber\LongLivedSandboxSubscriber records the timestamp of the last PostCreateEvent in state (package_manager.last_create_event), and deletes the sandbox immediately when package_manager.settings:include_unknown_files_in_project_root transitions from TRUE/unset to FALSE. Hook\CronHook (a #[Hook('cron')] implementation) compares that timestamp against Settings::get('package_manager_max_sandbox_age', 14) (in days) and deletes the sandbox if it's stale and not currently locked. getSandboxDirectory() and getStagingRoot() were also relaxed to work without an active lock (needed since cron and the config subscriber must locate the directory outside of a claimed stage), but getStagingRoot() only caches its result in the shared tempstore when a lock is actually held, to avoid polluting shared state from incidental lookups.

Upgrade

Code that calls SandboxManagerBase::getSandboxDirectory() before creating or claiming a stage will no longer get a \LogicException; it now returns the deterministic sandbox path directly. Code that relied on destroy() deleting the sandbox directory (or on the package_manager_cleanup queue running shortly after) must not assume the directory is gone until cron has run and the configured package_manager_max_sandbox_age has elapsed. Sites that need faster or slower cleanup can set, for example:

// settings.php
$settings['package_manager_max_sandbox_age'] = 7; // days

Summary

Drupal's installer used to install the database driver module (for databases other than core's built-in drivers, such as PostgreSQL) as a separate, dedicated step before any other module was installed. This issue removes that special case: the database driver module is now installed together with the rest of the site's modules, using the same batch installation process, while still guaranteeing it goes in first and triggers the container rebuild it needs. This is an internal installer change with no effect on how sites are built or configured.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The dedicated call to module_installer->install([$provider], TRUE) inside drupal_install_system() in install.inc is removed. Instead, a new helper _install_get_database_module_name() in install.core.inc inspects the active database connection (via Database::getConnection()->getProvider() and its autoload option looking for src/Driver/Database/) to determine whether the database is provided by a driver module rather than core. If so, install_profile_modules() prepends that module to the list of modules to install with array_unshift(), and install_recipe_required_modules() marks it as required so it sorts to the front of the batch alongside modules flagged required in their .info.yml.

This relies on the container_rebuild_required info key mechanism (introduced for the related change in #3614153, which did the same for the System module). pgsql.info.yml now sets container_rebuild_required: true, so install_profile_modules()'s batch grouping logic in install.core.inc puts the driver module in its own batch group and rebuilds the container before and after installing it, the same way any other module can request a rebuild, rather than through installer-specific code.

A follow-up, #3618797, was filed to replace the remaining _install_get_database_module_name() helper with Database::getConnection()->getProvider() directly.

item.title: #3616277: Deprecate several locale functions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +477/−347 · php +475/−347 · yml +2
  • Diff: d5f08dc
  • Discussion: #3616277 · 5 contributors · 31 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

As part of converting the locale module to object-oriented code, six procedural helper functions in locale.module are now deprecated: locale_translation_use_remote_source(), locale_string_is_safe(), locale_translatable_language_list(), locale_js_translate(), locale_translation_language_table(), and locale_is_translatable(). Calling any of them now triggers a deprecation notice, and they will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Most gained a direct service or static-method replacement; two (locale_translation_use_remote_source() and locale_translation_language_table()) have no replacement because their logic was inlined into the code that used to call them. This only affects code that calls these functions directly (custom or contributed modules); regular site administrators are not affected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural functions locale_string_is_safe(), locale_translatable_language_list(), locale_is_translatable(), locale_js_translate(), locale_translation_language_table(), and locale_translation_use_remote_source() are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in 13.0.0.
  • New API: New Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages service (getTranslatableLanguages(), isTranslatable()) and new Drupal\locale\LocaleXss class (stringIsSafe()) replace the deprecated locale functions.

Technical details

The deprecated function bodies now just call the new location and stay as thin wrappers that raise E_USER_DEPRECATED. locale_string_is_safe() moved verbatim to LocaleXss::stringIsSafe(). locale_translatable_language_list() and locale_is_translatable() moved to the new LocaleLanguages service (getTranslatableLanguages() and isTranslatable()). locale_js_translate() moved to the new LocaleJs::jsTranslate() service, but that class is marked @internal, so the deprecation message points to a service that isn't part of the committed public API. locale_translation_language_table()'s logic was moved into a new TranslationStatusForm::translationLanguageTable() method and wired up as the form's #after_build callback instead of the old procedural callback. locale_translation_use_remote_source() had no natural home, so every caller was changed to inline the underlying config check ($config->get('locale.settings')->get('translation.use_source') == LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL) directly.

Introducing LocaleLanguages (and, in one case, LocaleJs) as an injected dependency required adding a new constructor parameter to numerous locale classes that previously called the procedural functions: several services (LocaleFetch, LocaleProjectChecker, LocaleSource, LocaleConfigManager, LocaleFileManager), forms (ExportForm, ImportForm, TranslateFormBase, TranslationStatusForm), hook classes (LocaleHooks, LocaleFormHooks, LocaleThemeAlterHooks, a new LocaleThemeAlterHooks split out of the old LocaleFormHooks), LocaleRequirements, and the LocaleConfigSubscriber event subscriber. Several of these classes were also modernized to constructor property promotion in the same pass. LocaleThemeAlterHooks is a newly split-out class holding the hook_js_alter() and hook_library_info_alter() implementations that used to live in LocaleFormHooks, and it now injects LocaleJs via an #[AutowireServiceClosure] to avoid a hard circular/unnecessary dependency.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions:

// Before
locale_string_is_safe($string);
locale_translatable_language_list();
locale_is_translatable($langcode);
locale_js_translate($files, $language);

// After
\Drupal\locale\LocaleXss::stringIsSafe($string);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages::class)->getTranslatableLanguages();
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages::class)->isTranslatable($langcode);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->jsTranslate($files, $language);

For locale_translation_use_remote_source() and locale_translation_language_table(), there is no replacement API; inline the equivalent logic:

// Before
locale_translation_use_remote_source();

// After
\Drupal::config('locale.settings')->get('translation.use_source') == LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL;

If a custom or contributed module extends any of the affected locale classes (for example TranslateFormBase, ExportForm, ImportForm, TranslationStatusForm, LocaleFetch, LocaleSource, LocaleConfigManager, LocaleProjectChecker, LocaleFileManager, or LocaleConfigSubscriber) and overrides its constructor, add the new LocaleLanguages $localeLanguages constructor argument (no backward-compatibility shim was added for these on main).

catch, who committed the change, noted that the JS translation logic was ported to LocaleJs as-is rather than being redesigned per #2607376 and #3525743, but accepted this because the moved code is explicitly marked @internal. berdir reviewed multiple iterations and contributed specific naming and structural suggestions (his own words: "I contributed quite a bit with specific suggestions on naming and so on"), and daffie's near-RTBC review prompted nicxvan to update the issue summary and change record, which had drifted out of date. item.title: #3614825: Allow additional modules to be installed alongside the profile modules
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task

  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +122/−43 · php +109/−43 · yml +13

Summary

Drupal's test runner used to install a test's install profile first, then make a second call to install any extra modules listed in the test's static $modules property (and the default theme), each of which rebuilds the service container. This change lets those extra modules and the default theme be installed in the same pass as the profile's own modules and themes, cutting the number of container rebuilds during test setup and speeding up the test suite. There is no behavior change for site owners; it only affects how Drupal core and contrib tests execute. As part of the change, the method some test classes override to add modules, installModulesFromClassProperty(), is deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: FunctionalTestSetupTrait::installModulesFromClassProperty() is deprecated in Drupal 12.0.0 and removed in 13.0.0; override getModulesFromClassProperty() instead to supply extra modules for a test.

Technical details

install_profile_modules() and install_profile_themes() in install.core.inc now read $install_state['extra_modules'] and $install_state['default_theme'] and merge them into the profile's own module and theme lists before making a single call to the module/theme installer, instead of installing the profile first and the extras separately. install_install_profile() also writes default_theme into system.theme config when present.

On the test side, FunctionalTestSetupTrait::installParameters() now populates those two install_state keys from a new getModulesFromClassProperty() method (which just returns the modules collected recursively from static::$modules) and from $this->defaultTheme. installDrupal() no longer calls installModulesFromClassProperty()/installDefaultThemeFromClassProperty() after the profile install step, because the extra modules and theme are now installed as part of the profile install itself. installModulesFromClassProperty() remains as a deprecated BC wrapper around getModulesFromClassProperty() for the few callers, such as PerformanceTestTrait, that still invoke it directly. WebDriverTestBase and PerformanceTestBase were switched from overriding installModulesFromClassProperty() to overriding getModulesFromClassProperty().

Because path_alias can now be installed in the same batch as another module that creates a path alias from its own hook_install(), PathAliasRepository::pathHasMatchingAlias() now catches DatabaseException and returns FALSE instead of fataling when its own table doesn't exist yet; a related edge case involving route-dependent modules is tracked separately in #3616642. Several test-only modules gained explicit dependencies in their .info.yml files (e.g. on layout_builder) because they could no longer rely on being installed after the module they depend on.

Upgrade

Test classes that override installModulesFromClassProperty() to add extra modules should override getModulesFromClassProperty() instead:

// Before:
protected function installModulesFromClassProperty(ContainerInterface $container): void {
  self::$modules = [
    'js_testing_ajax_request_test',
    'js_testing_log_test',
  ];
  parent::installModulesFromClassProperty($container);
}

// After:
protected function getModulesFromClassProperty(): array {
  $modules = parent::getModulesFromClassProperty();
  $modules = array_merge($modules, ['js_testing_ajax_request_test', 'js_testing_log_test']);
  return $modules;
}

installModulesFromClassProperty() still works but triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and will be removed in Drupal 13.

item.title: #3614401: Allow install profiles to opt out of being installed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +155/−11 · php +117/−10 · yml +38/−1
  • Diff: 6a4608b
  • Discussion: #3614401 · 3 contributors · 20 comments

Summary

Install profiles can now declare that they should never be installed as a module in their own right. Adding opt_out_install: true to a profile's .info.yml tells the installer to skip the step where the profile itself is enabled after its modules and configuration are in place. This is aimed at minimal profiles used for testing or automated environments that have no hooks of their own to run, so there is no reason to keep them installed as a module. Drupal core's own testing and testing_nightwatch profiles are now marked this way.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New opt_out_install key in an install profile's .info.yml lets the profile skip being installed as a module at the end of the installer.

Technical details

The installer reads each profile's parsed info array into $install_state['profile_info'] (via install_profile_info()). install_install_profile() in install.core.inc now checks $install_state['profile_info']['opt_out_install'] before calling \Drupal::service('module_installer')->install() on the profile itself, skipping that call when the key is truthy. drupal_install_system() in install.inc was likewise updated so that the core.extension config's profile key is cleared (not just when there is no profile at all) whenever the profile has opted out, keeping the stored configuration consistent with the fact that the profile was never installed as a module.

Because the core testing profile is used by hundreds of tests and now opts out, several tests that relied on the testing profile's optional configuration (a body field on node, and a locale config override) had to be reworked: the body field was extracted into a new body_field test module, and a new testing_locale profile was added that still gets installed and carries the locale-specific config for the handful of tests that depend on it. A new testing_skip_install profile, whose hook_install() throws an exception, was added purely as test coverage (#3614401's ProfileSkipInstallTest) to prove the opt-out path never runs the profile's install hook. This work builds on #3614153, which moved the System module install step earlier in the installer.

Upgrade

Add opt_out_install: true to an install profile's .info.yml if the profile has no hook_install() or other behavior that depends on being installed as a module:

name: My minimal profile
type: profile
opt_out_install: true

Profiles that rely on optional configuration tied to the profile's own module weight, or that implement install hooks, should not set this key.
